content:
The latest stable release v4.6.0 for Lean is out now!

The release brings:

  • improvements for writing termination proofs
  • custom simplification procedures
  • viewing the call hierarchy in VSCode
  • improvements to pretty printing

as well as many bug fixes to Lean and Lake.

But you shouldn't be satisfied with that short summary: you should go and read the blog post announcing the release and explaining these new features in more detail: https://lean-lang.org/blog/2024-2-29-lean-460/

(The new blog posts are written using Verso, Lean's upcoming documentation tool.)

We encourage everyone using previous stable releases to update their repositories to v4.6.0.

Std, Aesop, and Mathlib are all now available for v4.6.0, as well as lean4checker and lean-repl.

  • the stable branch on each repository has been updated to use v4.6.0
  • there is a v4.6.0 tag in each repository if you would like to pin to a commit using this toolchain.

We are intending to create the release candidate for v4.7.0, with many new features, early next week.

v4.6.1 is now available, which is identical to v4.6.0 except for a significant performance improvement in server startup time. (~50% for many users.) This was a regression since v4.5.0.

(Std/Aesop/Mathlib will shortly move to v4.7.0-rc1, which also includes this improvement.)
